subject.title: Add a retraction window for forwarded exec approvals (agent-cancellable hold before prompt delivery)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in pre-delivery hold/retract contract for forwarded exec approvals, and where should that contract live?
rationale: The request changes approval safety semantics, config, Gateway protocol/RPC, forwarding channels, and Codex/native approval boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Design core hold/retract
options.body: Open a maintainer-owned design for a Gateway-level opt-in hold/retract contract that preserves the issue's fail-open/fail-closed safety constraints.

options.title: Decline retraction window
options.body: Keep immediate prompt delivery as the product guarantee and close this as not planned after explaining the approval-audit tradeoff.

options.title: Pursue agent-side mitigation
options.body: Avoid a public retraction RPC and instead reduce junk prompts through agent prompting, auto-review, or command-shaping improvements.

recommendation.title: Design core hold/retract
recommendation.body: Open a maintainer-owned design for a Gateway-level opt-in hold/retract contract that preserves the issue's fail-open/fail-closed safety constraints.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared approval framework history makes this the best available owner signal for the protocol and manager contract decision.
